_comment: pypi.org stays reachable on purpose: a sandbox where a user cannot
piplite.install('something') in their own notebook is much less useful, and that is
It is safe to leave on because the thing it used to paper over is fixed properly:
this flavour ships a *patched* osw, and it now carries a distinct local version
(2.8.2+pyodide1), so pypi's plain 2.8.2 can never be substituted for it. Before the
stamp the two tied and the released copy won - which still requires dask
unconditionally and therefore cannot install in Pyodide at all.
The vendored index is still complete enough for a cold start without the network
(see KERNEL_SEEDS in scripts/resolve_wheels.py); the fallback is a convenience for
the user's own packages, not a dependency of the sandbox itself.
